content_summary: Account posted content sexualizing a minor in a costume context.
original_violation_reason: CSAM / sexualization of a minor — zero tolerance.
user_appeal_statement: I didn't mean anything by it, it was just a cosplay photo of my niece.
rationale: Zero-tolerance policy applies regardless of claimed intent; the content objectively sexualizes a minor per the evidence.

content_summary: Sealed Post captioned 'unlock to see something you won't believe 🔥' that, once unlocked, contained an unrelated recipe video.
original_violation_reason: Engagement-baiting on Sealed Posts with deceptive unlock promises.
user_appeal_statement: It's just marketing, everyone does teaser captions.
rationale: Caption implies a specific dramatic reveal; the unlocked content is unrelated — this is the exact example the guidelines call out.

content_summary: Sealed Post caption said 'unlock for a surprise'; the unlocked content was a different but topically related dance video from the same creator.
user_appeal_statement: My caption was generic, not deceptive, and the content matches my usual style.
rationale: A vague-but-not-deceptive caption paired with genuinely related content doesn't meet the 'deceptive unlock promise' bar the guidelines describe — the automated flag overreached.

content_summary: Comment thread where a user posted another user's full home address and phone number after a dispute.
original_violation_reason: Doxxing — sharing private information without consent.
user_appeal_statement: That info is publicly available on their old business listing.
rationale: Guidelines prohibit sharing private information without consent regardless of whether it's findable elsewhere; posting it in a hostile context after a dispute is textbook doxxing intent.

content_summary: User replied to a creator's post with sharp but on-topic criticism of their editing choices, no personal attacks.
original_violation_reason: Flagged by another user as harassment.
user_appeal_statement: I was critiquing their content, not attacking them personally.
rationale: Guidelines explicitly encourage 'constructive feedback... respectful critiques'; the content described contains no targeting or bullying, just criticism — looks like report abuse, not real harassment.

content_summary: Video caption used a known slur targeting an ethnic group, repeated three times for emphasis.
original_violation_reason: Hate speech — slurs and dehumanizing language.
user_appeal_statement: It's a word used commonly in music lyrics I was quoting.
rationale: Guidelines prohibit slurs outright; quoting-as-defense doesn't change that the slur was posted and reached the platform's audience.

content_summary: Post satirizing a political figure's policy positions using exaggerated caricature, no reference to protected characteristics.
original_violation_reason: Reported as hate speech by multiple users.
user_appeal_statement: This is political satire about policy, not about any protected group.
rationale: Guidelines define hate speech as attacking protected characteristics; policy-position satire about a public figure doesn't meet that bar even if provocative — looks like report brigading, not an actual violation.

content_summary: Video depicts two adult performers in explicit sexual activity, no protective label applied.
user_appeal_statement: I marked it as Sensitive Content — Nudity.
rationale: Guidelines are explicit that sexually explicit content is never permitted 'regardless of category' of sensitive-content labeling — the label doesn't cure the underlying prohibition.

content_summary: Photo of a fine-art nude sculpture, marked Sensitive Content — Nudity by the user at upload.
user_appeal_statement: I labeled it correctly per the guidelines, it's artistic and non-explicit.
rationale: Guidelines explicitly carve out 'artistic nudity' as a valid Sensitive Content category, and the user complied with the labeling requirement — this is an auto-flag needing confirmation, not an actual violation.

content_summary: User re-uploaded another creator's full video with only a different caption and no attribution on the post itself.
original_violation_reason: Copyright infringement — claiming others' work as your own.
user_appeal_statement: I gave credit in the comments.
rationale: A buried comment credit doesn't cure a full unauthorized re-upload presented on the post itself as the appellant's content.

content_summary: Post claims a specific home remedy cures a serious illness, cites no source, presented as factual medical advice.
original_violation_reason: Health misinformation that could cause harm.
user_appeal_statement: It's just my personal experience/opinion, not medical advice.
rationale: Genuinely contested: personal-anecdote framing vs. factual-claim framing is a real gray area the guidelines don't resolve cleanly, and the consequences of getting it wrong in either direction are real — warrants human review.

content_summary: Video shows a user performing a stunt with visible safety precautions (harness, spotters, padded surface) and a verbal disclaimer not to attempt it.
original_violation_reason: Dangerous challenge that could cause harm.
user_appeal_statement: I included every safety precaution and a disclaimer, this isn't reckless content.
rationale: Guidelines target dangerous challenges as a class, but visible safety measures and an explicit disclaimer meaningfully change the risk profile — closer to stunt content with precautions than a viral dangerous-challenge video.

content_summary: A Watch Together session was hijacked mid-stream by a co-host who played unrelated explicit content without the host's consent.
original_violation_reason: Host's account was flagged for the incident.
user_appeal_statement: I didn't share that content, my co-host did without my knowledge.
rationale: Guidelines specifically define this violation as 'hijacking a Watch Together party to share content the host did not authorize' — the violation as written is attributable to the hijacker, not the host; the wrong account was actioned.

content_summary: Investigation found 6 accounts sending coordinated gifts to a single account from the same device and payment method over a 2-week period.
original_violation_reason: Self-gifting through alternate accounts to extract payouts.
user_appeal_statement: Those are my friends' accounts, they just like supporting me.
rationale: A coordinated gifting pattern from the same device/payment method across multiple accounts is precisely the evidentiary signature the guidelines describe for self-gifting rings; 'friends supporting me' doesn't explain the shared device and payment method.

content_summary: A non-consensual intimate image of an ex-partner posted with a caption naming them.
user_appeal_statement: They're my ex, I have the right to post photos of my own relationship.
rationale: Guidelines prohibit non-consensual intimate imagery outright regardless of the poster's relationship to the subject; consent to the relationship isn't consent to post intimate images.

content_summary: Original artwork post got auto-flagged by a keyword filter for containing the word 'kill' in an unrelated caption ('this outfit kills it').
original_violation_reason: Automated keyword match for violent language.
user_appeal_statement: It's a common expression, not a threat.
rationale: Clear keyword-filter false positive — no actual violent content or threat present, idiomatic usage the automated system isn't equipped to distinguish.

content_summary: Post reviews and compares over-the-counter supplement brands, including standard dosing info printed on the product labels.
user_appeal_statement: These are legal OTC supplements, this is a product review.
rationale: Guidelines target illegal drugs/substances specifically; legal OTC supplement reviews citing label-printed dosing don't fall under that category — an overbroad automated flag.

content_summary: Post argues against a specific piece of legislation affecting a religious group's practices, framed around policy/legal reasoning, with one sentence near the end expressing personal distrust of 'people like them'.
user_appeal_statement: This is a policy argument, the one line was taken out of context.
rationale: Mostly legitimate policy discourse but contains a genuinely borderline dehumanizing generalization — not clearly a slur/attack, not clearly innocuous either. Reasonable reviewers could disagree; appropriate for human escalation rather than automated confidence in either direction.
